items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: I had, uh, Alvin Alcorn on trumpet.

ctx.x: Well, I had, uh, one time I had, uh, Alvin Alcorn on trumpet. Was that in the beginning, I mean, when you first formed? Yes. Yeah? I had, uh, Willie Pardew on second trumpet. And I had, uh, Lee Collins on third trumpet. I had, uh, Raymond Brown on trombone. Uh-huh. I had David Jones on tenor sax. I was playing fourth, I was playing fourth, Alton, Bodley on third, Alton. Who was that? Bodley. Bodley? Yeah. I don't remember him. Well, him and H.E. was raised up together. Was that his first name or second name? No,…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: He had some nice trumpet players around here like ... Alvin Alcorn

ctx.x: I never knew him, but I heard a lot of guys talk about him.

Well, he was a summons on him, Red Happy. He used to, he was with John Robichaud. Oh man. He was a fine drummer, this guy, Black Benny, was a fine drummer. He got killed, a poison or something. I think he got killed. He had some nice trumpet players around here like Buddy Petit, Ricka, Rene, Chris Kelly, Lee Collins, Alvin Alcorn, Manny Mineta.
What are these different guys specialize in?

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: And Alvin Alcorn was playing with me on the Pelican.

ctx.x: Well, he had a little bit of air on the piano. But play. Ooh, he could play some piano. And never was sober. Never was sober. He stayed right there in the same hotel with us. He wake up in the morning and get drunk. Get drunk when he eat. Twelve o'clock he get drunk. Go to work he's drunk. Come from work he's drunk. But play. Never was late on the job. And never went to sleep. Never went to sleep. But he'd be drunk. Played everything you put in front of him and what you don't put in front of him he played. He was…
